**My reasoning:**

I have been farming this land in Quzhou for over fifty years. My father farmed it before me. I know one system that works here — winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same ground. That is what I will do again.

I have about 6 mu of land that I can still manage at my age. My son is in the city. My wife helps during busy times, but the heavy work I hire out now. My back is not what it was.

For wheat, I buy improved seeds from the village supply shop — not the most expensive, but they know me there and the seeds are reliable. I put down compound fertilizer before planting and add urea in spring. I irrigate four times: before planting to wet the soil, the winter water in December, then jointing, then grain filling. I spray once in spring for weeds and rust. I use rotary tillage — the rotary machine is easier to hire locally and does the job.

After wheat harvest in June, I plant maize straight into the stubble — I stopped deep ploughing for maize years ago, it wastes time and money. Everyone uses hybrid maize seeds now, even I know that much. I irrigate a couple of times if rain is short. I topdress urea once at the big bell stage.

I do not grow cotton anymore. Too much work and the price has been bad. A small patch of vegetables near the house for eating, but that does not count as a crop plan.
